findings.statement: Established ccRCC drug target (HIF-2alpha). Open Targets association score [gene=EPAS1; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.4871]. Tractability is small molecule (SM: Approved Drug) and PROTAC-type; BELZUTIFAN is at APPROVAL. Nuclear transcription factor (heterodimerises with ARNT; regulates VEGF). Reactome includes HIF gene-expression regulation and PD-L1 transcription. DepMap shows a modest ccRCC-selective dependency (selectivity [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3]; not a common essential; the BH q-value is just above the usual cut-off, so borderline). PRISM compound PT-2385 (Phase 1, a single-target compound) is not significantly selective in 2D culture, as expected for HIF-2 biology.

Top Open Targets ccRCC association (rank 1 among the top-25 list). Driver status is confirmed: nonsynonymous mutation frequency in the combined CPTAC and TCGA cohort, recurrent, BH q-value near zero [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.483]. UniProt: E3 ligase subunit that recruits hydroxylated HIF under normoxia; also negative regulator of mTORC1 via RPTOR. It is a loss-of-function tumour suppressor, so it is a mechanism and stratification gene, not a direct drug target; it is the upstream rationale for HIF-2alpha inhibition (belzutifan).

Rank 1 in the convergence ranking, with strongly tumour-up, purity-robust and TCGA-replicated expression. Open Targets association is modest (score [gene=CA9; type=open_targets_association; source=Open Targets Platform; score=0.3088], mostly literature, no genetic or somatic evidence). Tractability covers antibody (AB: Advanced Clinical), small molecule (SM: Approved Drug) and PROTAC-type. Drugs as returned: GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_3, IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB PHASE_2, SULTHIAME PHASE_4, ETHOXZOLAMIDE WITHDRAWAL. UniProt: cell membrane and microvillus membrane, so it is accessible to antibodies and imaging. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (not selective), so it works as a surface targeting handle and imaging or diagnostic biomarker, not as a functional dependency. The PRISM best compound (para-toluenesulfonamide) has several annotated targets [gene=CA9; type=prism_response; source=DATASET:PRISM-20Q2; compound_targets=4] and is uninformative about CA9 alone.

Convergence rank 4. Cell-membrane ligand of CD27 (UniProt), strongly tumour-up in TCGA and purity-robust. Tractability: antibody (AB: Advanced Clinical) and other clinical modalities. Drugs as returned: CUSATUZUMAB PHASE_2, VORSETUZUMAB PHASE_1, VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN PHASE_1, MDX-1411 PHASE_1. Open Targets association is low, with literature support only. DepMap selectivity is near zero [gene=CD70; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.006] (no dependency; not common essential), so this is a tractable surface antigen for ADC or cell-therapy, not a functional dependency.

Convergence rank 30, with tumour-up, purity-robust expression. Plasma-membrane ecto-enzyme (apical cell membrane, also secreted form) that hydrolyses extracellular nucleotides and cGAMP. Tractability: AB, small molecule (SM: High-Quality Ligand) and OC. Drug: AGS-16C3F (antibody-drug conjugate) at PHASE_2. No DepMap ccRCC dependency (not selective, not common essential), so it is an antigen-type target, not a dependency. Open Targets association is low.

MCT4 lactate exporter, a basolateral cell-membrane protein (UniProt), strongly tumour-up and purity-robust in ccRCC. Tractability labels include antibody-type localisation, small-molecule binder and high-quality ligand, but no approved or clinical drug is returned. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (not selective, not common essential) and no PRISM compound is annotated to it. This is a tractable but untested gene, and the dependency case is weak.

Convergence rank 8 and the highest biomarker score among the leading genes: tumour-up, purity-robust, with adverse prognostic signal (TCGA Cox significant) and grade association. Cytoplasmic methyltransferase that consumes S-adenosylmethionine and shapes epigenetic methylation (UniProt). No drug is returned from Open Targets. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency, so it is a candidate prognostic or tumour-intrinsic biomarker, not a validated dependency. Because it is cytoplasmic, it is not an antibody target.

Convergence rank 6, with the genetic-association component of Open Targets (listed in the top-25 disease targets) plus tumour-up protein and RNA. Cell-membrane and caveolar HDL receptor (UniProt), so it is accessible. Tractability is predicted but no drug is returned. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (not selective, not common essential). Tractable but untested; the dependency case is weak.

Convergence rank 3. Strongly down in tumour (proximal tubule loss) with favourable prognostic association in TCGA; cytosolic glycolytic and fructolytic enzyme with a reported tumour-suppressor adapter role (UniProt). No drug is returned and DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency. This is a downregulation biomarker (loss of normal proximal-tubule identity), not a drug target.

Convergence rank 5. Proximal-tubule organic anion transporter, strongly down in ccRCC tumour with favourable prognostic association. Drugs returned (as substrate/inhibitor annotations): PROBENECID PHASE_4, PRATOSARTAN PHASE_3. These do not reflect ccRCC therapeutic rationale. A downregulation biomarker, not a target, and no dependency evidence.

Convergence rank 2, strongly tumour-up (RNA and protein) and purity-robust, with literature support. Drugs returned (ME-344 PHASE_1_2, metformin entries at WITHDRAWAL) are generic mitochondrial-pathway annotations, not gene-specific. Open Targets association is low. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency. Treat as a tumour-specific biomarker candidate, not a target.

Established ccRCC drug target (mTOR inhibitors, as in everolimus and temsirolimus use). Open Targets lists it among the top-25 disease associations; it was not scored further here because it is outside the leading convergence list. Included as a reference to separate established targets from the new candidates.

Established ccRCC drug target (VEGFR2, the main target of the anti-angiogenic tyrosine kinase inhibitors). It is among the top-25 Open Targets associations. It was not profiled in detail (not in the leading convergence list); included to anchor the known-target class.

caveats: Open Targets association scores for new convergence leaders (CD70, ENPP3, NNMT, SLC16A3, COXFA4L2, ALDOB) are low and mostly literature-driven, so they should not be read as genetic validation.

No leading convergence candidate except EPAS1 shows a selective DepMap ccRCC dependency (and EPAS1 is borderline, BH q about 0.06). The surface antigens CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are antibody or cell-therapy targets, not functional dependencies; druggability without dependency is a weaker case.
PRISM 2D screens miss HIF-2 biology, and the CA9 PRISM compound has several annotated targets, so neither is informative about the gene alone.
Drug lists are as returned by Open Targets and include non-oncology annotations (for example probenecid, metformin, sulthiame, withdrawn compounds); they do not imply ccRCC activity.

MTOR and KDR were not profiled with DepMap, mutation or UniProt calls because of the tool-call budget; their role rests on Open Targets association and prior clinical knowledge. STRING interactors were not queried.
Statement text in several findings about tumour-up and prognosis directions comes from the convergence ranking components, not from numerically annotated records.
